question: In the underground gas storage cycles, why did gas withdrawal in cycles 1 to 4 show a positive net mass transfer rate (net gas-to-oil transfer)?
expect: premise false: withdrawal showed a negative NMRT, −0.357 mL/MPa (oil-to-gas, vaporization/extraction); injection was the positive one, 0.115 mL/MPa (abstract)
rendered:
=== Phase Behavior and Mass Transfer During Oil Reservoir Conversion to Underground Gas Storage: Effects on Storage Capacity and Recovery Efficiency, page 7 ===

According to the text, during gas withdrawal in cycles 1 to 4, the net mass transfer rate was positive, indicating a net gas-to-oil transfer. This is because the gas phase volume increased, and the oil phase saturation decreased. The interphase mass transfer was mainly based on the evaporation and extraction of the oil phase, supplemented by the condensate dissolution of the gas phase.
